program.summary: Cheek Middle School Band is the largest organization on campus. It serves more than 280 students in grades 6 through 8. The directors' 2026 Music for All biography describes three concert ensembles, jazz band, beginning instrument classes, and an active percussion program.
program.feeder: Cheek Middle School Band is a feeder for the Braswell High School Band.
program.placeNote: The school address is 200 Denton Way, Aubrey, Texas 76227. The directors describe the program as Cheek Middle School in Prosper, in the Denton Independent School District.

directors.name: Dr. Gregory L. Denson
directors.photoAlt: Dr. Gregory Denson, Director of Bands
directors.photoCredit: Portrait published in the 2026 Music for All National Festival program.
paragraphs: Gregory L. Denson is Director of Bands at Cheek Middle School in the Denton Independent School District. The Cheek program is the largest organization at the school. In the 2026 Music for All festival program he described it as three concert ensembles, jazz band, and an active percussion program, serving more than 280 students in grades 6 through 8. The Honors Band was selected to perform at the 2026 Music for All National Festival in Indianapolis.

Dr. Denson is a native of Morven, Georgia. He holds a Bachelor of Music from Morehouse College, a Master of Music Education with teacher certification from The Florida State University, and a Doctor of Philosophy in Music Education from Georgia State University. He has studied with David Morrow, Uzee Brown, Andre Thomas, Richard Clary, Clifford Madsen, Steve Kelly, Kimberly VanWeelden, Pat Meighan, Clarence Johnson, and Gholnescar Muhammad.

He began his teaching career at D. M. Therrell High School in the Atlanta Public Schools. Students there took part in the Georgia Music Educators Association Large Group Performance Evaluation, college homecoming parades, the University of Georgia JanFest Clinic, and community and civic events. He was co-director of the Atlanta Public Schools Superintendent Jazz Ensemble and lead middle school band teacher for Atlanta Public Schools.

Before Cheek, he was Director of Bands at East Cobb Middle School in Marietta, Georgia. Under his direction that program grew from 120 students to more than 580 in four years, with five concert ensembles, jazz band, and student-led chamber ensembles. The East Cobb Honors Band was a featured ensemble at the Music for All National Festival in 2023, the Georgia Music Educators Association In-Service in 2023, and the University of Georgia Midfest Honor Band in 2020 and 2021. Those honors belong to East Cobb, not to Cheek.

He has presented clinics at the Midwest Clinic and the GMEA In-Service Conference. The biography on the band's Google Site also lists him as a Conn-Selmer VIP, an educational ambassador for the Eastman Music Company, and a former chair of the Georgia Music Educators Association Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Access Committee. He serves on the executive board of the Minority Band Directors National Association and is active as an adjudicator, guest conductor, and clinician.

directors.name: Daney E. Glover
directors.photoAlt: Daney Glover, Associate Director of Bands
directors.photoCredit: Portrait published in the 2026 Music for All National Festival program.
directors.note: This role and biography are the ones the program published on its Google Site and in the March 2026 Music for All program. The campus band directory page fetched for this site listed Dr. Denson and Eithan Moreno, and did not list Mr. Glover. Confirm the current staff list before the next school year.
paragraphs: Daney E. Glover is named Associate Director of Bands in the biography the program published and in the March 2026 Music for All festival program. At Cheek, that biography says he conducts the Symphonic Band, teaches beginning saxophone, trumpet, trombone, euphonium, and tuba, and assists with the Jazz, Concert, and Honors Bands. His festival biography describes the program as serving over 300 students and as the largest organization on campus.
Before Cheek, he was assistant director of bands from 2018 to 2020 and director of bands from 2020 to 2023 at Cooper Middle School in Austell, Georgia, in the Cobb County School District.

He is an alumnus of Louisiana State University, where he was a member of the tuba and euphonium studio, the Golden Band from Tigerland, the Bengal Brass basketball band, the LSU Symphonic Band, the LSU Symphonic Winds, and the LSU Wind Ensemble. He studied euphonium and conducting with Dr. Joseph Skillen, Dr. Chasse Duplantis, Dr. Damon Talley, Dr. Dennis Llinàs, Dr. Kelvin Jones, Dr. Jaclyn Hartenberger, and Dr. Jack A. Eaddy Jr.

He played euphonium in the Cobb Wind Symphony under Alfred L. Watkins and has worked as a clinician with middle and high school bands in Georgia and the DFW metroplex. The published biography lists memberships in the Minority Band Directors National Association, the Texas Music Educators Association, the Texas Bandmasters Association, Kappa Kappa Psi, and Phi Beta Sigma.

beginning.who: The last published screening was for all incoming sixth graders and any current sixth or seventh graders who wanted to join band.

lastScreening.where: Cheek Middle School cafeteria, 200 Denton Way, Aubrey, TX 76227
notes: Families were told to enter through doors 12 and 13, across from the football stadium.
The program said that screening was the only date, that beginners had to be screened to be placed in a class, and that students who missed it would not be allowed to join.
A parent or guardian was asked to stay with the student. The visit was about 50 minutes.
Students rotated through instrument stations. The program asked them to try more than one instrument.

beginning.why: The program's published explanation is that people and instruments are different, and an instrument that is a poor fit makes band harder to enjoy. Specialists at each station help find the instrument a student is most likely to succeed on.

achievements.title: 2026 Mark of Excellence National Winner
achievements.summary: The Cheek Middle School Honors Band was named a 2026 Mark of Excellence National Winner in National Wind Band Honors, Band Class A. Denton ISD reported that only 16 other middle school band programs in the country received this award.
achievements.quote: These national accolades reflect the exceptional artistry, effort, and dedication of Denton ISD student musicians and educators. To have two of our programs recognized among the absolute finest in the country is a testament to the culture of excellence cultivated in our music classrooms every day.
achievements.quoteBy: Eddy Russell, Denton ISD Director of Fine Arts, October 2, 2026

achievements.title: Music for All National Festival, 2026
achievements.summary: The Honors Band was one of 52 scholastic ensembles invited to the 2026 Music for All National Festival, presented by Yamaha. Cheek performed on Friday, March 27, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. at the Howard L. Schrott Center for the Arts on the Butler University campus. Ensembles were chosen by recorded audition.

lessons.intro: The program describes private lessons as one of the fastest ways for a student to build individual skill. A teacher hears the student every week and can work on skills that a full-band rehearsal cannot cover one student at a time. Lessons can be before school, during band class, or after school, depending on the student and the teacher.
lessons.feeNote: The band Google Site lists private lessons at $20. Confirm the current fee with Dr. Denson before enrolling. This page will show a new number when it is updated in the site data file.
lessons.aid: Financial assistance is for families for whom lessons would cause undue hardship. It is not guaranteed, and it does not make lessons free. The program shares the cost with the family. Students who receive assistance agree to participate in band the following school year. Families who withdraw at the end of that year are responsible for repaying the scholarship amount.
lessons.contact: Questions and placement go through the directors. Email Dr. Denson. Personal emails for lesson teachers are not published on this site.
lessons.staffNote: Names and instruments below are the list published on the band Google Site under Personal Trainers. The directors should confirm that the list is still current. No private email addresses and no lesson-teacher photos are included.

practice.intro: Class-specific assignments, practice tracks, and method-book pages are not posted yet. Until the directors add them, this is a general practice pattern families can use. It is not a Cheek assignment.

steps.title: Set up the same way every day
steps.text: Put the music stand where the student can see it, check the reed or mouthpiece, and set a metronome before the first note.

steps.title: Warm up
steps.text: Long tones, a slow scale, and a few easy rhythms. Five quiet minutes here make the assignment easier.

steps.title: Work a short section
steps.text: Take the hardest four measures, play them slowly, and only speed up when they are correct three times in a row.

steps.title: Record one minute
steps.text: Play the passage once and listen back. Students hear rushing, missed notes, and tone more clearly than they do while playing.

steps.title: Pack up
steps.text: Swab or empty water, and put the instrument where it will leave the house for school.
